subject: [PATCH v3 02/11] mm, swap: support zswap and zeroswap as vswap backends

2026-08-06.patch_summary: This patch introduces support for virtual swap (vswap) in the Linux kernel, allowing pages to be compressed by zswap or detected as zero-filled without pre-allocating a physical swap slot. It builds on top of the existing swap-table infrastructure and supports zswap and zero-page backends. The vswap layer decouples PTE swap entries from physical backing, enabling efficient compression and detection of zero-filled pages. The patch also adds a sysctl to enable or disable vswap allocation at runtime and introduces a new build option for defaulting vswap on or off. However, it does not yet support physical disk backing or real writeback, which will be addressed in subsequent patches.

reviews.author: Youngjun Park
reviews.summary: Reviewer Youngjun Park questioned whether the vswap layer is actually enabled at populate time and suggested that only validation is needed to ensure it doesn't come in, specifically for free clusters (dynamic ci) where the cluster is freed immediately.
reviews.raw_body:
Hello Nhat

Does vswap actually come in at populate time?
For free clusters (dynamic ci), 
isn't the cluster freed immediately rather than going through this path?

If it is right, then just validation seems good enough. (assure vswap does not come in)

Thanks
Youngjun

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a mistake in cluster_reclaim_range() and agreed to fix it in the next version.
reviews.raw_body:
Acked. You're right I think. This got me staring at the code along
this direction, and I discovered another code path where I provisioned
for vswap's sake unnecessarily (cluster_reclaim_range()) - will fix
this in the next version.

Thanks for the review, Youngjun!

2026-08-15.patch_summary: This patch adds support for virtual swap (vswap) in the Linux kernel, allowing pages to be compressed by zswap or detected as zero-filled without pre-allocating a physical swap slot. The vswap layer is built on top of the existing swap-table infrastructure and supports zswap and zero-page backends. A new sysctl /proc/sys/vm/vswap_enabled is added to enable or disable vswap allocation at runtime, defaulting off unless configured otherwise. Existing virtual entries will continue to resolve their backend and drain naturally when vswap is turned off.
